newsitem.title: USA: FDA reviewers criticize PLC heart laser.
newsitem.headline: FDA reviewers criticize PLC heart laser.

text.p: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) reviewers on Monday cast doubt on the effectiveness of PLC Systems Inc's heart laser system as a treatment for patients with end-stage heart disease.

At an FDA advisory committee meeting, the reviewers said that positive data reported by the company could be due to a prolonged placebo effect. The reviewers also disputed some of PLC's study results.

Using the device, a surgeon drills 15 to 40 1-millimeter-wide channels in oxygen-starved tissue in the heart's left ventricle. The procedure is called Transmyocardial Revascularization (TMR), and is supposed to restore blood flow to damaged heart tissue.
PLC reported that one year after the procedure, 95 percent of the 97 patients who received TMR were free of angina, compared to only 30 percent of the 101 patients in the control group.

PLC said that, at the end of the trial, almost 80 percent of the TMR patients had not died, had a heart attack or unstable angina, or a recurrence of class IV angina. In contrast, it said 90 percent of the control group experienced one of these events.
But FDA reviewers disputed PLC's figures, saying that 31 percent of patient getting TMR died in the study compared to 13 percent of control patients. Panel reviewers also criticized PLC.
"I have never seen a clinical trial with so much missing data," said panelist Dr. Robert Califf of Duke University.
"How do you make statistical inferences when you are missing more than half the data?" Califf asked.
The agency's criticism is surprising, given that in September 1996 it judged the device safe and effective enough to let PLC treat all study patients with the device.
The panel is to debate the data further later Monday and make a recommendation for or against approval by the end of the day.
